questions.title: A main content of the pterygopalatine fossa
questions.question: Which of the following important nerves is one of the main contents found within the pterygopalatine fossa?

options.A: The thick and strong motor mandibular nerve
options.B: The specialized purely sensory optic nerve
options.D: The extremely long wandering vagus nerve

explanations.A: Incorrect. The mandibular nerve (CN V3) passes through foramen ovale into the infratemporal fossa, not through the pterygopalatine fossa, which belongs specifically to the maxillary division.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The optic nerve travels through the optic canal to reach the orbit and eye, taking no part in the pterygopalatine fossa.
explanations.C: Correct. The maxillary nerve (CN V2, the second, purely sensory division of the trigeminal nerve) crosses the pterygopalatine fossa on its way from the trigeminal ganglion to the face, entering through foramen rotundum and leaving through the inferior orbital fissure. It gives off major sensory branches to the face and upper teeth from within the fossa, making it one of the fossa's principal contents.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The vagus nerve (CN X) runs in the neck, thorax and abdomen, supplying parasympathetic and visceral sensory fibres far from the skull-base pterygopalatine fossa.

questions.learning_objective: Name the maxillary nerve as a main content of the pterygopalatine fossa, entering via foramen rotundum.
